outline: Nephropathic cystinosis — CTNS/cystinosin lysosomal cystine transport
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
discipline: Renal Physiology / Molecular Genetics / Metabolic Disease
diagnosis: Nephropathic cystinosis causing renal Fanconi syndrome
mechanism: CTNS encodes cystinosin, a lysosomal membrane transporter that moves cystine from the lysosomal lumen into the cytoplasm. Loss of cystinosin causes lysosomal cystine accumulation and crystal formation in many tissues; proximal tubular cell dysfunction produces generalized Fanconi syndrome.
vignette: An 18-month-old boy is evaluated for poor growth, polyuria, polydipsia, and recurrent dehydration. Examination shows widening of the wrists and bowed legs. Laboratory studies show hypophosphatemia, hypokalemia, a normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, glucosuria despite a normal serum glucose concentration, and generalized aminoaciduria. Slit-lamp examination shows cystine crystals in the cornea.
lead: Which of the following cellular defects most directly explains this child's disorder?
correct: Failure of lysosomal cystine export due to loss of cystinosin, causing intracellular cystine accumulation and proximal tubular dysfunction
distractors: Failure of apical cystine and dibasic amino acid reabsorption in proximal tubules, causing excessive urinary cystine excretion
Loss of OCRL phosphatidylinositol phosphatase activity, producing an oculocerebrorenal syndrome with proximal tubular dysfunction
Excess fibroblast growth factor 23 signaling, causing renal phosphate wasting with suppression of calcitriol production
Direct mitochondrial toxicity in proximal tubular cells caused by chronic tenofovir exposure
distractor_notes: Defects in the apical cystine/dibasic amino acid transporter cause cystinuria and recurrent cystine nephrolithiasis. They do not cause lysosomal cystine accumulation, corneal crystals, or the systemic Fanconi phenotype of cystinosis.

OCRL deficiency can cause Lowe syndrome with proximal tubular dysfunction, but it is associated with congenital ocular abnormalities and neurologic impairment rather than corneal cystine crystals from lysosomal storage.
FGF23 excess causes renal phosphate wasting and rickets/osteomalacia, but it does not produce generalized proximal-tubule wasting with glucosuria, aminoaciduria, and corneal cystine deposition.
Tenofovir can cause acquired proximal tubular mitochondrial injury and Fanconi syndrome, but this toddler's corneal cystine crystals and inherited multisystem phenotype point to cystinosis.
key_expl: This child has nephropathic cystinosis. CTNS encodes cystinosin, the lysosomal membrane transporter that exports cystine into the cytoplasm. Loss of cystinosin causes lysosomal cystine accumulation and crystal formation in multiple tissues. Proximal tubular injury produces generalized Fanconi syndrome, explaining bicarbonate, phosphate, potassium, glucose, and amino-acid wasting; phosphate wasting contributes to rickets and poor growth. Corneal cystine crystals are a highly characteristic clue.
objective: Explain nephropathic cystinosis as a CTNS/cystinosin defect that prevents lysosomal cystine export, causing cystine accumulation and renal Fanconi syndrome.
